excerpts: **Governing rule:** only the secure (Blizzard-signed) execution path may call protected functions — cast a spell, use an item, target a unit, or show/hide/move a protected frame in combat.
Addon Lua is *insecure*; it can only pre-configure secure templates **out of combat** and let the player's hardware click do the protected work.
A button inheriting `SecureActionButtonTemplate` reads *attributes* on click and performs the matching protected action inside Blizzard's secure handler.
`RunMacroText`, `CastSpellByName`, `UseAction`, `TargetUnit`, etc. are protected: from a tainted path they are no-ops that raise `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED`.
There is no API to "cast a spell from a timer/event" — that would let an addon auto-play the character.
The only sanctioned route is **hardware-event → secure-template**: a real key/mouse press whose secure handler reads attributes and performs exactly one action.
**What taint is.** Every value and execution context carries a secure/insecure bit.
Blizzard's shipped code is secure; your addon's code and every value it produces are *tainted*.
WoW Lua starts secure; the moment execution reads addon code or data, that execution becomes tainted ("addon code is sticky; anything it touches becomes sticky").
Taint persists until `/reload` or logout.
*Execution taint* — if a tainted function is anywhere on the call stack when a protected function runs, the action is blocked.

*Value taint* — a tainted value written into a Blizzard-owned table/variable taints that variable; later secure code reading it becomes tainted (sticky — the classic cause of `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` naming your addon for a bug that surfaces frames away).

*Hooks* — a plain hook running your code inside Blizzard's path spreads taint. Use `hooksecurefunc` (post-hook runs *after* the secure call and receives a copy of the call's **arguments** — not its return values; observing those args is taint-safe). Reading is fine; writing back into protected state is not.
`InCombatLockdown()` returns true from `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` (combat start) until `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` (combat end).
While true, any insecure attempt to set a security-sensitive attribute, re-parent/move/show/hide a protected frame, or call a protected function is **blocked** and raises `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED`.
Bail at the top of any function that touches protected state: ```lua function MyAddon:UpdateLayout() if InCombatLockdown() then return end ... end ```

`RegisterStateDriver(frame, "stateid", macroConditional)` tells the **secure** environment to watch a macro-conditional and write `state-<stateid>` on the frame whenever the result changes — *including in combat*, because evaluation and the attribute write happen entirely inside Blizzard's restricted environment.

**release.sh** generates an addon zip file from a Git, SVN, or Mercurial checkout.

**release.sh** works by creating a new project directory ( `.release` by default), copying files from the checkout into the project directory, checking out external repositories then copying their files into the project directory, then moves subdirectories into the project root.
The project directory is then zipped to create a distributable addon zip file which can also be uploaded to CurseForge, WoWInterface, Wago, and GitHub (as a release).

**release.sh** can read a **.pkgmeta** file and supports the following directives. See the [wiki page](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager/wiki/Preparing-the-PackageMeta-File) for more info. _externals_ (Git, SVN, and Mercurial) Caveats: An external's .pkgmeta is only parsed for ignore and externals will not have localization keywords replaced. _ignore_ _plain-copy_ _license-output_ _changelog-title_ _manual-changelog_ _move-folders_ _package-as_ _enable-nolib-creation_ (defaults to no) Caveats: nolib packages will only be uploaded to GitHub and attached to a release. Unlike with the CurseForge packager, manually uploaded nolib packages will not be used by the client when users have enabled downloading libraries separately. _enable-toc-creation_ (defaults to no) Create game type specific TOC files from your TOC file if you have multiple `## Interface-[Type]:` lines. _tools-used_ _required-dependencies_ _optional-dependencies_ _embedded-libraries_ Note: All fetched externals will be marked as embedded, overriding any manually set relations in the pkgmeta.

**release.sh** supports the following repository substitution keywords when copying the files from the checkout into the project directory. See the [wiki page](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager/wiki/Repository-Keyword-Substitutions) for more info. _@ [localization](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager/wiki/Localization-Substitution) (locale="locale", format="format", ...)@_ _escape-non-ascii_ _handle-unlocalized_ _handle-subnamespaces="concat"_ _key_ _namespace_ _same-key-is-true_ _table-name_ _@file-revision@_ _@project-revision@_ _@file-hash@_ _@project-hash@_ _@file-abbreviated-hash@_ _@project-abbreviated-hash@_ _@file-author@_ _@project-author@_ _@file-date-iso@_ _@project-date-iso@_ _@file-date-integer@_ _@project-date-integer@_ _@file-timestamp@_ _@project-timestamp@_ _@project-version@_ _@build-date@_ _@build-date-iso@_ _@build-date-integer@_ _@build-timestamp@_

Build type keywords Specific keywords used in a comment at the start ( `@keyword@` ) and end ( `@end-keyword@` ) of a block of code can be used to conditionally run that code based on the build type. If the build type does not match, the block of code is comment out so line numbers do not change. Supported keywords and when the code block will run: `alpha` : in untagged builds. `debug` : never. Code will only run when using an unpackaged source. `do-not-package` : never. Same as `debug` except removed from the packaged file. `no-lib-strip` : _(not supported in Lua files)_ in any build other than a _nolib_ build. `retail` , `version-retail` , `version-classic` , `version-bcc` , `version-wrath` , `version-cata` , `version-mists` : based on game version. `do-not-package` is a bit special. Everything between the tags, including the tags themselves, will always be removed from the packaged file. This will cause the line numbers of subsequent lines to change, which can result in bug report line numbers not matching the source code. The typical usage is at the end of Lua files surrounding debugging functions and other code that end users should never see or execute. All keywords except `do-not-package` can be prefixed with `non-` to inverse the logic.
**release.sh** uses the TOC file to determine the package name for the project.

Building for multiple game versions **release.sh** automatically detects what game version(s) the addon supports. You only need to run a build once and the file will be tagged with the appropriate versions when uploaded.

Multiple TOC files You can create [multiple TOC files](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/TOC_format) , one for each supported game type, and **release.sh** will use them to set the build's game version. Single TOC file **release.sh** can support multiple game versions with the use of additional `## Interface-[Type]` lines in your TOC file.

Using TOC file creation (splitting) When using multiple `## Interface-[Type]` lines in a single TOC file, you can use the `-S` command line option or add `enable-toc-creation: yes` to your `.pkgmeta` file to automatically generate game type specific TOC files using your existing preprocessing logic. The fallback TOC file will use the base interface value as it's version. For each `## Interface-[Type]` line, a new TOC file is created. In the above example, **release.sh** would create `MyAddon_Vanilla.toc` and `MyAddon_Cata.toc` , based on `MyAddon.toc` applying each game type's processing logic and rewriting the interface version and also copy `MyAddon.toc` processed as retail.

Using comma separated interface values The game client for 10.2.7 and 4.4.0 have added the option to specify multiple interface versions delimited by commas. ``` Interface: 11502, 100207, 40400, 110000 ``` The above example would mark an addon compatible with the latest version of all client flavors and The War Within alpha. Other game client versions will stop processing the line when it hits the comma, So until Classic Era also supports multiple versions, if you include the Classic Era interface version first, all three game clients will load the addon correctly. That said, just because you _can_ include a bunch of interface versions doesn't mean you _should_ start adding upcoming versions you haven't tested your addon against.

Uploading **release.sh** uses following environment variables for uploading: `CF_API_TOKEN` \- a [CurseForge API token](https://authors.curseforge.com/#/settings/api-tokens) , required for the CurseForge API to fetch localization and upload files. `WOWI_API_TOKEN` \- a [WoWInterface API token](https://www.wowinterface.com/downloads/filecpl.php?action=apitokens) , required for uploading to WoWInterface. `WAGO_API_TOKEN` \- a [Wago Addons API token](https://addons.wago.io/account/apikeys) , required for uploading to Wago Addons. `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` \- a [GitHub personal access token](https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens) , required for uploading to GitHub.

Dependencies **release.sh** is mostly POSIX-compatible, so it should run in any Unix-like environment provided the following are available: bash >= 4.3 awk grep sed curl zip version control software as needed: git >= 2.13.0 subversion >= 1.7.0 mercurial >= 3.9.0 (pre-3.9 will have issues with [secure connections](https://www.mercurial-scm.org/wiki/SecureConnections) ) [jq](https://stedolan.github.io/jq/download/) >= 1.5 (when uploading)

excerpts: Description: Generate an addon zip file from a Git, SVN, or Mercurial checkout. - BigWigsMods/packager
**release.sh** generates an addon zip file from a Git, SVN, or Mercurial checkout.

**release.sh** works by creating a new project directory ( `.release` by default), copying files from the checkout into the project directory, checking out external repositories then copying their files into the project directory, then moves subdirectories into the project root.
The project directory is then zipped to create a distributable addon zip file which can also be uploaded to CurseForge, WoWInterface, Wago, and GitHub (as a release).

**release.sh** can read a **.pkgmeta** file and supports the following directives. See the [wiki page](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager/wiki/Preparing-the-PackageMeta-File) for more info. _externals_ (Git, SVN, and Mercurial) Caveats: An external's .pkgmeta is only parsed for ignore and externals will not have localization keywords replaced. _ignore_ _plain-copy_ _license-output_ _changelog-title_ _manual-changelog_ _move-folders_ _package-as_ _enable-nolib-creation_ (defaults to no) Caveats: nolib packages will only be uploaded to GitHub and attached to a release. Unlike with the CurseForge packager, manually uploaded nolib packages will not be used by the client when users have enabled downloading libraries separately. _enable-toc-creation_ (defaults to no) Create game type specific TOC files from your TOC file if you have multiple `## Interface-[Type]:` lines. _tools-used_ _required-dependencies_ _optional-dependencies_ _embedded-libraries_ Note: All fetched externals will be marked as embedded, overriding any manually set relations in the pkgmeta.

**release.sh** supports the following repository substitution keywords when copying the files from the checkout into the project directory. See the [wiki page](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager/wiki/Repository-Keyword-Substitutions) for more info. _@ [localization](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager/wiki/Localization-Substitution) (locale="locale", format="format", ...)@_ _escape-non-ascii_ _handle-unlocalized_ _handle-subnamespaces="concat"_ _key_ _namespace_ _same-key-is-true_ _table-name_ _@file-revision@_ _@project-revision@_ _@file-hash@_ _@project-hash@_ _@file-abbreviated-hash@_ _@project-abbreviated-hash@_ _@file-author@_ _@project-author@_ _@file-date-iso@_ _@project-date-iso@_ _@file-date-integer@_ _@project-date-integer@_ _@file-timestamp@_ _@project-timestamp@_ _@project-version@_ _@build-date@_ _@build-date-iso@_ _@build-date-integer@_ _@build-timestamp@_

Build type keywords Specific keywords used in a comment at the start ( `@keyword@` ) and end ( `@end-keyword@` ) of a block of code can be used to conditionally run that code based on the build type. If the build type does not match, the block of code is comment out so line numbers do not change. Supported keywords and when the code block will run: `alpha` : in untagged builds. `debug` : never. Code will only run when using an unpackaged source. `do-not-package` : never. Same as `debug` except removed from the packaged file. `no-lib-strip` : _(not supported in Lua files)_ in any build other than a _nolib_ build. `retail` , `version-retail` , `version-classic` , `version-bcc` , `version-wrath` , `version-cata` , `version-mists` : based on game version. `do-not-package` is a bit special. Everything between the tags, including the tags themselves, will always be removed from the packaged file. This will cause the line numbers of subsequent lines to change, which can result in bug report line numbers not matching the source code. The typical usage is at the end of Lua files surrounding debugging functions and other code that end users should never see or execute. All keywords except `do-not-package` can be prefixed with `non-` to inverse the logic.
**release.sh** uses the TOC file to determine the package name for the project.

Building for multiple game versions **release.sh** automatically detects what game version(s) the addon supports. You only need to run a build once and the file will be tagged with the appropriate versions when uploaded.

Multiple TOC files You can create [multiple TOC files](https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/TOC_format) , one for each supported game type, and **release.sh** will use them to set the build's game version. Single TOC file **release.sh** can support multiple game versions with the use of additional `## Interface-[Type]` lines in your TOC file.

Using TOC file creation (splitting) When using multiple `## Interface-[Type]` lines in a single TOC file, you can use the `-S` command line option or add `enable-toc-creation: yes` to your `.pkgmeta` file to automatically generate game type specific TOC files using your existing preprocessing logic. The fallback TOC file will use the base interface value as it's version. For each `## Interface-[Type]` line, a new TOC file is created. In the above example, **release.sh** would create `MyAddon_Vanilla.toc` and `MyAddon_Cata.toc` , based on `MyAddon.toc` applying each game type's processing logic and rewriting the interface version and also copy `MyAddon.toc` processed as retail.

Using comma separated interface values The game client for 10.2.7 and 4.4.0 have added the option to specify multiple interface versions delimited by commas. ``` Interface: 11502, 100207, 40400, 110000 ``` The above example would mark an addon compatible with the latest version of all client flavors and The War Within alpha. Other game client versions will stop processing the line when it hits the comma, So until Classic Era also supports multiple versions, if you include the Classic Era interface version first, all three game clients will load the addon correctly. That said, just because you _can_ include a bunch of interface versions doesn't mean you _should_ start adding upcoming versions you haven't tested your addon against.

Uploading **release.sh** uses following environment variables for uploading: `CF_API_TOKEN` \- a [CurseForge API token](https://authors.curseforge.com/#/settings/api-tokens) , required for the CurseForge API to fetch localization and upload files. `WOWI_API_TOKEN` \- a [WoWInterface API token](https://www.wowinterface.com/downloads/filecpl.php?action=apitokens) , required for uploading to WoWInterface. `WAGO_API_TOKEN` \- a [Wago Addons API token](https://addons.wago.io/account/apikeys) , required for uploading to Wago Addons. `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` \- a [GitHub personal access token](https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens) , required for uploading to GitHub.

Dependencies **release.sh** is mostly POSIX-compatible, so it should run in any Unix-like environment provided the following are available: bash >= 4.3 awk grep sed curl zip version control software as needed: git >= 2.13.0 subversion >= 1.7.0 mercurial >= 3.9.0 (pre-3.9 will have issues with [secure connections](https://www.mercurial-scm.org/wiki/SecureConnections) ) [jq](https://stedolan.github.io/jq/download/) >= 1.5 (when uploading)

content.tbc_anniversary_packaging_and_the_20506_:
The `.toc` file tells WoW which client family and UI version an addon targets. The `Interface` number is used to classify an addon as out of date when it is older than the current client [tbc_anniversary_packaging_and_the_20506_constraint[0]] [1] [tbc_anniversary_packaging_and_the_20506_constraint[0]] [1]. For this project, use a TBC-specific TOC only after checking the live client. The evidence shows TBC Anniversary releases using `20506` in filenames, including `AtlasLootTBC Anniversary ... 20506-11509.zip`, and associating the file with Classic TBC [tbc_anniversary_packaging_and_the_20506_constraint[1]] [9]. However, that page does not formally state that `20506` is Blizzard's Interface value [tbc_anniversary_packaging_and_the_20506_constraint[1]] [9].

| Artifact | Purpose | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `GuildCeremony.toc` | TBC Anniversary | Put the verified TBC Interface line and TBC load metadata here. |
| `GuildCeremony_Classic.toc` | Classic Era | Use a separately verified Classic value and API assumptions. |
| `GuildCeremony_Forever.toc` | Future Forever | Add only after beta/live testing confirms the TOC and APIs. |
| Release ZIP | Distribution | Make one clearly labeled artifact per client family. |

Do not fix an out-of-date warning merely by telling users to enable the load-out-of-date option. That can bypass the warning but cannot restore missing APIs, changed event payloads, or incompatible XML/UI behavior. Test each artifact on a clean client, confirm that the folder contains the TOC at its root, and display the detected client/build in the addon diagnostics.
content.guild_communication_and_star_topology_sy:
Register a short prefix with `C_ChatInfo.RegisterAddonMessagePrefix`; recipients must register it before receiving `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` [guild_communication_and_star_topology_sync[0]] [2]. The API limits the prefix to 16 characters and the message to 255 characters [guild_communication_and_star_topology_sync[0]] [2]. Use `C_ChatInfo.SendAddonMessage(prefix, message, chatType, target)`. For a guild ceremony, `GUILD` is the normal broadcast and `OFFICER` is suitable for coordinator commands; `WHISPER` can target a specific participant [guild_communication_and_star_topology_sync[0]] [2]. Do not depend on custom `CHANNEL`, which is disabled on Classic [guild_communication_and_star_topology_sync[0]] [2].

A two-client star topology should be deliberately small:

| Role | Responsibility | Failure behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Coordinator | Owns ceremony phase, epoch, and roster snapshot | Re-election after timeout. |
| Participant A | Sends local intent and receives state | Shows stale-state warning after timeout. |
| Participant B | Same as A | Requests a snapshot rather than guessing. |
| Optional observer | Receives read-only updates | Never becomes coordinator automatically without an election rule. |

Use a compact envelope such as `v=1|epoch=12|seq=44|op=PHASE|value=welcome`. Every state-changing packet should carry a protocol version, ceremony ID, epoch, sender, sequence, and operation. The coordinator broadcasts a state snapshot; clients acknowledge the highest sequence they applied. Duplicate sequence numbers are ignored, old epochs are rejected, and a new coordinator increments the epoch. Since the API only confirms enqueueing and messages are throttled [guild_communication_and_star_topology_sync[0]] [2] [guild_communication_and_star_topology_sync[0]] [2], the UI must say `pending`, `confirmed`, or `offline` rather than claiming delivery.

Throttle-safe behavior is more important than visual immediacy. Coalesce repeated updates, send only on phase changes, cap retries with exponential spacing implemented by a queue, and fall back to local display when guild transport is unavailable. Keep a human-readable officer or guild-chat instruction as an optional backup, but do not automatically spam chat.
content.savedvariables_and_ceremony_state:
Saved variables are plain Lua data written between sessions [savedvariables_and_ceremony_state[0]] [11]. Account-wide data belongs in the account `SavedVariables` directory; per-character data belongs under the realm and character directory [savedvariables_and_ceremony_state[0]] [11]. A sensible schema is:

```lua
GuildCeremonyDB = {
  version = 1,
  ceremonies = {},       -- account-wide definitions
  preferences = {},      -- account-wide UI preferences
  characters = {},       -- character-local opt-in and display state
  lastSeenEpoch = {},    -- per-guild or per-ceremony anti-replay state
}
```

Treat saved data as untrusted input. Validate types, cap string lengths, discard unknown operations, migrate by explicit version, and write only after a local change. Never use SavedVariables as a distributed database: two clients can log out with divergent copies, and saved data does not prove that another player received a packet. The coordinator's runtime state should be authoritative for the current session, with a snapshot request for recovery.
content.ui_taint_combat_lockdown_and_the_non_neg:
Secure execution is required for protected actions such as casting, using items, targeting, or manipulating protected frames in combat [ui_taint_combat_lockdown_and_the_non_negotiable_safety_boundary[0]] [10]. Addon code and values are tainted, and taint can propagate into Blizzard-owned state [ui_taint_combat_lockdown_and_the_non_negotiable_safety_boundary[0]] [10]. During `InCombatLockdown()`, insecure code cannot change security-sensitive attributes or move, show, hide, or re-parent protected frames [ui_taint_combat_lockdown_and_the_non_negotiable_safety_boundary[0]] [10]. Protected calls from tainted paths can produce `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` [ui_taint_combat_lockdown_and_the_non_negotiable_safety_boundary[0]] [10].

A ritual addon must therefore be a social state machine, not a gameplay controller. It may show text, icons, timers, participant status, ceremony phases, acknowledgements, and opt-in prompts. It may let a player click an ordinary, unprotected button to advance their own local ceremony UI. It must not cast, target, use items, accept invitations, change equipment, move protected frames, or automate any combat or protected action. It must not schedule a timer that performs a protected action, and it must not hide combat errors by swallowing blocked-action diagnostics.

If a future design uses a secure action button, configure it only out of combat and require the player's hardware click. The ceremony feature itself should not need secure templates at all. Keeping it outside the secure UI path reduces taint risk and makes Classic Era, TBC Anniversary, and possible Forever ports easier.
content.common_failure_modes_and_tests:
| Failure | Likely cause | Defensive test or remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Addon marked out of date | Wrong Interface number or wrong client artifact | Test the TOC on the actual client; publish separate artifacts. |
| Loads but errors on login | API or event payload changed | Run a clean-profile smoke test and guard optional APIs. |
| No messages received | Prefix was not registered, wrong event, or wrong channel | Register on load, handle `CHAT_MSG_ADDON`, and log protocol version. |
| Messages intermittently vanish | Throttle, logout, reload, disconnect, or invalid target | Queue, coalesce, acknowledge, retry, and show pending state. |
| Guild sync splits into two ceremonies | Stale coordinator or missing epoch handling | Use monotonic epoch and sequence numbers; request a fresh snapshot. |
| Officer controls affect everyone unexpectedly | Trusting any sender | Authorize by guild rank or explicit coordinator election, then validate every operation. |
| UI breaks in combat | Protected frame mutation or taint | Use ordinary frames; guard `InCombatLockdown()` before protected work. |
| Settings appear lost | Wrong SavedVariables scope or migration bug | Test account and character scopes independently and version the schema. |
| Users install the wrong build | Ambiguous ZIP/folder names | Include client family in artifact and project labels and test the ZIP root. |

Include tests for solo mode, two clients in the same guild, absent coordinator, reload during a ceremony, reconnect, duplicate packets, old packets, full throttle, combat start during a phase change, and clean installation from CurseForge and Wago.
content.bigwigs_packager_curseforge_and_wago:
BigWigs packager generates an addon ZIP from a source checkout and supports uploads to CurseForge, Wago, WowInterface, and GitHub releases [bigwigs_packager_curseforge_and_wago[0]] [5]. Its multi-game packaging capability is useful here because Classic Era and TBC Anniversary should not share an untested artifact [bigwigs_packager_curseforge_and_wago[1]] [13]. Put packaging metadata in source control, derive the release version from a tag, and use substitutions for the version and client-specific TOC values. The packager documentation and examples show that multiple game-version TOCs can be generated, including Classic-style suffixes and interface substitutions [bigwigs_packager_curseforge_and_wago[2]] [6].

A practical pipeline is: lint Lua; run a local smoke test; build one ZIP per client family; inspect the ZIP root and TOC; upload tagged artifacts to CurseForge and Wago; retain the GitHub release as the canonical source record. Label TBC Anniversary explicitly. Do not imply that CurseForge or Wago distribution makes an addon compatible with every Classic client: the current project listings themselves show separate Classic-family files and client-specific releases [bigwigs_packager_curseforge_and_wago[3]] [7].
content.classic_era_tbc_anniversary_and_forever_:
Classic Era and TBC Anniversary are separate compatibility targets even when their addon APIs look similar. TBC Anniversary evidence includes client lines such as 2.5.5 and 2.5.6 and release labels containing `20506` [classic_era_tbc_anniversary_and_forever_strategy[0]] [9]. That is enough to justify a TBC test matrix, not enough to assume every Classic API, event, or TOC suffix is interchangeable.

Forever should be treated as a third target. The official Forever page confirms a beta beginning September 17, 2026 [classic_era_tbc_anniversary_and_forever_strategy[1]] [3], and the supplied launch evidence reports November 4, 2026 [classic_era_tbc_anniversary_and_forever_strategy[2]] [12]. The cited official material does not establish that Forever shares TBC's Interface number, addon restrictions, SavedVariables layout, or communication behavior. Maintain a compatibility adapter for TOC values, chat registration, event names, and UI capabilities, then validate those assumptions during beta. Do not promise Forever support based only on its branding as a Classic-style game.
content.synthesis:
The safest design is deliberately conservative across three dimensions. First, transport: guild broadcast is convenient but throttled and not delivery-confirmed, so a coordinator plus acknowledgements is stronger than peer-to-peer guesses. Second, state: account SavedVariables are useful for definitions and preferences, but live ceremony state belongs in a versioned runtime protocol, not in files that may diverge. Third, UI authority: ordinary social frames are portable, while protected actions introduce combat lockdown and taint constraints with little benefit to a ceremony feature.

The main tension is between ceremony immediacy and platform safety. A rich ritual experience wants automatic sequencing, visible timers, and synchronized actions; WoW's security model requires player agency for protected behavior. The correct compromise is automatic synchronization of information and explicit player clicks for optional social actions, never automation of gameplay. The same boundary also improves portability: an informational, non-protected addon is more likely to survive differences among Classic Era, TBC Anniversary, and Forever.

The release strategy follows the same principle. One source tree can support several client families, but only through separately tested TOCs, explicit capability checks, and clearly labeled artifacts. Ship TBC Anniversary first with the verified live-client value, keep Classic Era compatibility independent, and make Forever a beta branch until Blizzard's actual client behavior is known.
